== 1. THE CPU COLUMN IS NOW OUTPUT TOKENS PER WALL SECOND ==
The old fifth column was `ps -o time= | awk -F: '{print $NF}'`, which keeps only the LAST colon-separated field of cumulative CPU time. Reproduced directly: `echo 1:20.93 | awk -F: '{print $NF}'` -> 20.93 (the brief's live 2026-08-23 measurement: 80.9 s rendered as 20.9), and `echo 1:02:03 | awk -F: '{print $NF}'` -> 03 — 62 minutes of CPU displayed as three. Two rows were not comparable at all. A CORRECT CPU number would still have been the wrong metric: measured CPU utilisation of these API-driven workers is 6.9% (T817), 9.7% (T801), 8.1% (T808), so ~92% of elapsed is spent waiting on the provider and local CPU tracks how a model chose to search (grep, git, python, JSON parsing), not how much work it did. Replaced with output tokens per wall second: `tokens_out` from untracked/tokens/tokens.jsonl over `ps` elapsed. New helper rate_of(tokens_out, elapsed) is exposed under the WATCH_FLEET_SOURCE guard (the nap_for_age pattern) so the arithmetic is unit-pinned, and it reproduces the operator's worked values: 127683/1232 = 103.6/s and 407129/3400 = 119.7/s (dsflash, brief cites 102.7 and 119.2 off ps elapsed rather than claimed->done), 157457/2162 = 72.8/s (dspro, brief cites 72.0). LABEL: the value carries a '/s' suffix, so no one can read 103.6/s as CPU seconds; there is no column header on this surface to label (T738 removed the banner), so the label is in the value.
MISSING READINGS: UNKNOWN, never 0 and never stale. 'Never 0' is rate_of's (an empty reading or a zero elapsed returns UNKNOWN, and a rendered 0.0/s can therefore only mean a real recorded zero). 'Never stale' is the join's: a reading whose ts predates the task's CURRENT `claimed` belongs to a previous run of the same id and is dropped rather than divided by this run's elapsed. On the live store today every PROGRESS row renders UNKNOWN, which is correct — no in-flight task has a meter reading (T820 15 records, T814 39, T818 1, all with tokens_out null; T771/T821 none at all).
STORE FIELDS: `managent status --json` carries neither `agent` nor `claimed` (printStatusJson omits them), so both are now merged in from the store — the same reason tools/fleet-keeper.sh:639-642 reads the store directly for claim_count.

== A DEFECT I INTRODUCED AND THE ARM CAUGHT ==
My first rate rendering was '%.1f/s' unconditionally, which made an outlier (12000 tokens over a 1 s worker) render '12000.0/s' — 9 chars in an 8-char slot. Arm O caught it on the first green run. Truncating the value to fit the column would have been the SAME defect this column replaced (a silently dropped digit group), so the fix is the format, not the slot: one decimal below 1000/s (real rates are 60-150), none at or above, which fits any plausible value in 8 chars. Arm O now pins 999 -> '999.0/s', 1000 -> '1000/s', 12000 -> '12000/s' and asserts every rendered form is <= 8 chars; it also reads the rate BY FIELD rather than by column slice, because a slice is what hid the overflow. Absurd values (>= 10^7/s, non-physical) would widen the row and push the description right — visible misalignment is honest, a truncated number is not.

Not touched, not hidden, still red in the suite.
METER `ts` IS NOT RUN IDENTITY (new, found while building the staleness guard). The guard compares a reading's `ts` to the task's `claimed`, which is a PROXY for run identity, not run identity. The proxy is weaker than it looks: `ts` means different things per source — records with source 'pi-session-jsonl-retro' carry the pi session file's timestamp, not the write time, so e.g. T322's only reading (711 tokens, ts 2026-08-03T17:11:06Z) predates its claim (23:29:40Z) and is dropped. Census on the live meter: 483 tasks have at least one non-null tokens_out; 137 have a reading surviving the guard; 346 have only pre-claim readings; 452 individual readings dropped. DASHBOARD IMPACT TODAY: none — the rate column renders only on PROGRESS rows (live workers), and all 346 are long-done tasks. The failure mode is also the safe one (UNKNOWN, never a wrong number), which is why the guard stays. But the honest fix belongs to the meter, not the display: tokens.jsonl should carry the run identity (claim epoch or session id) that a join can key on, at which point the display can drop the ts heuristic. Secondary nit in the same area: ts strings are compared lexicographically and some carry fractional seconds ('2026-08-23T10:47:35.328Z'), which sorts BEFORE '...35Z' — a sub-second edge case that can only push a reading toward UNKNOWN, never toward a wrong rate. Owner: the token-meter row (T751 territory), not this one.
A frame can legitimately contain the text '(more)' after this change — T823's own title is 'dashboard: rate, holder, no (more)', so it renders in the OPEN/CONCERNS description. Grepping a LIVE frame for '(more' is therefore not a valid check; arms K and N grep scratch stores whose descriptions are 'row NN'.

== COMMIT BLOCKED BY A FOREIGN STAGED INDEX (not a defect in this work) ==
tools/git-commit-mine REFUSED the commit: the shared .git/index already held 65 staged paths belonging to another console — T818's docs/infra/task-corpus-b/* (11 chunks x 5 model files, derive.py, manifest.json, notes.md) and findings/T818-corpus-b.json. That is the T268 incident class the wrapper exists to make impossible, and the wrapper's own instruction is 'do NOT unstage another console's work; wait for its owner to commit, then retry'. I did not unstage it, and I did not reach for --explicit, which would have swept T818's corpus into a commit labelled T823. The wrapper had staged my four paths before refusing, so I unstaged MINE (git restore --staged) to leave the index exactly as I found it — 65 foreign paths, none of mine — rather than leave my work sitting where another console's commit would absorb it under the wrong message.
STATE AT CLOSE: all four deliverables are complete and verified in the WORKING TREE, uncommitted (untracked/watch-fleet.sh M, tools/regression-watch-fleet.sh M, findings/T823-dashboard-truth.json and findings/T823-context.json untracked). Every predecessor on this file (T469, T492, T493, T591, T738, T739, T799, T804) landed as its own commit, and this one should too. Once T818's staged set lands, the commit is one command:
  tools/git-commit-mine untracked/watch-fleet.sh tools/regression-watch-fleet.sh findings/T823-dashboard-truth.json findings/T823-context.json --task T823 -m '<message>'
Precedent for a seat committing a worker's delivered-but-uncommitted change: 8980219 (T493, 'Worker stalled after delivering; committed by the seat from its staged index + findings').
SECOND-ORDER HAZARD OBSERVED WHILE BLOCKED (worth recording, cost me a false alarm): at 22:41Z, with my deliverables uncommitted, another console ran a `git stash`/`git stash pop` round trip (HEAD reflog shows the lone 'reset: moving to HEAD' that stash's internal reset leaves). During that window the working tree read as CLEAN — `git status` empty for my paths, `git diff HEAD` empty, my edits absent from both files, T818's 65 staged paths and its whole docs/infra/task-corpus-b/ directory gone from disk — and I concluded the work had been destroyed by a hard reset. It had not: the pop restored everything (both files' content and mtimes at 22:42:43Z, the 65 staged paths, T818's corpus, findings/T818-corpus-b.json), and the suite re-ran 15/16 with arm F alone red, identical to the pre-stash run. Nothing was lost and nothing needed re-applying. The lesson is not about stash: it is that an UNCOMMITTED deliverable in a shared working tree is readable as absent by anyone who looks during another console's stash window, so 'my file is at HEAD and git status is clean' is not sufficient evidence that work was destroyed — re-read before concluding, which is the same absence-is-not-evidence rule the operator has already ruled on for status assertions. It is also a second argument for landing this commit as soon as the index frees: the window only exists while the work is uncommitted.
